reference: GNU coreutils readlink from the isolated reference PATH is the independent oracle for parity cases, including stdout bytes and exit status. Bash type/help metadata is checked separately against the documented readlink builtin registration and source help text.
coverage: Default mode reads literal relative and dangling symlink targets; a regular file failure checks aggregate status and successful output from multiple operands.
An option-like pathname after --, --no-newline output, and NUL-delimited output with a newline inside a link target.
-f canonicalization through a symlink with dot-dot components, including an absent final component.
-e canonicalization of an existing symlink path and failure on a missing operand.
-m lexical canonicalization through a missing prefix, plus verbose missing-path diagnostics.
Bash builtin type and help metadata contract.
exclusions: No absolute host paths, devices, network peers, credentials, privileged operations, destructive inputs, or system state are used.
No deferred case is needed: readlink operates on ordinary relative fixtures and GNU coreutils provides a matching reference.

cases.purpose: Read relative and dangling symlinks without resolving their targets, continue after a regular-file failure, and return failure if any operand is not a symlink.
cases.script: ln -s 'target with spaces' 'relative link'; ln -s 'absent/file' dangling; : > regular; readlink 'relative link' dangling regular

cases.purpose: Use -- to treat a symlink named -n as a pathname rather than an option.
Verify --no-newline suppresses the output delimiter while preserving following shell output.
cases.script: ln -s 'target text' link; readlink --no-newline link; printf '[end]\n'

cases.purpose: Verify -z emits NUL delimiters for multiple links and preserves an embedded newline in a symlink target.
cases.script: ln -s $'line\nbreak' first; ln -s 'second target' second; readlink -z first second

cases.purpose: Resolve a relative symlink and dot-dot components with -f, and allow a missing final path component when its parent exists.
cases.script: mkdir -p real/sub; : > real/file; ln -s real alias; readlink -f alias/sub/../file alias/sub/not-created

cases.purpose: Resolve an existing path with -e, omit a missing operand from stdout, and return failure when any operand does not exist.
cases.script: mkdir -p real/sub; : > real/file; ln -s real alias; readlink -e alias/sub/../file absent

cases.purpose: Canonicalize lexically with -m through a missing prefix and normalize dot and dot-dot components.
Check that -v reports a missing-path diagnostic, emits no path result, and returns failure. Diagnostic prefixes identify the builtin and are outside byte comparison.
Check Bash reports readlink as a builtin and exposes the documented readlink help, including its canonicalization modes.
cases.script: [[ $(type -t readlink) == builtin ]] || exit 1; help_text=$(help readlink); [[ $help_text == *'Read a symbolic link or canonicalize a path.'* ]] || exit 2; [[ $help_text == *'--canonicalize-missing'* ]] || exit 3; printf 'builtin\nhelp documents canonicalization\n'
